fixed.summary: A text shadow draws every layer of its list, as CSS's text-shadow does: up to eight, painted last first under the fill, each with its own offset, blur and colour, each transitioning as a box shadow's layer does. Before, a TSX text kept only the widest layer. This changes what the theme classes with several layers mean: Tailwind's text-shadow-sm, -md and -lg now draw all their layers. A layer in currentColor (or with no colour) or contrast-color(currentColor) takes the ink of each text it reaches, as CSS inherits the keyword, so a halo written once on a HUD's root rings every text in its own contrast.

Their halo over the scene is text-shadow-tag (the style's --tag-halo) instead of text-shadow-2xs: the 81 texts that wrote text-shadow-2xs, which is Tailwind's 1 px drop at 15 % black and read about 1.1:1 over a white sky, now draw the eight-copy ring in contrast-color() of their ink, in TSX as the CSS path draws var(--tag-halo). OrbMeter's caption, which sits under the orb on the scene, takes the halo too instead of text-shadow-xs's soft drop. text-shadow-2xs itself is unchanged; a game that wrote it for a halo should write text-shadow-tag.

added.summary: The theme halo class text-shadow-tag: the default pack carries --tag-halo (eight unblurred copies 1 to 1.5 px round the glyphs in contrast-color() of the ink) as textShadow.tag, and a pack's theme may set its own textShadow entries, each a CSS text-shadow list.
